newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases on reduced demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases on reduced demand.

text.p: Prices of key shares fell slightly on reduced demand at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Wednesday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The NSE 20-share index was down 0.67 points to stand at 3073.36. Turnover was posted at 16.856 million shillings traded on 369,316 shares from 26.185 million shillings traded on 715,787 shares.
Activity in the market was dominated by financials for the second day in the week. Kenya Commercial Bank traded heavily at 78 from 79 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 47 from 46.75.
"Today's price on KCB fell because there was only one foreign investor buying, as compared to Tuesday, when there were two competing buyers," a broker said.
Barclays Bank was stable at 97 unchanged, while National Bank of Kenya traded at 13.50 from 13.80.

"Almost all the financials traded in the morning. In fact if this demand for KCB is sustained, investors will start looking at the other leading competing banks listing in the market," a senior banker said.
Demand in the agriculturals improved slightly with foreigners buying Kakuzi at 98 from 99.50 and 500 shares of Sasini Tea & Coffee at 60.50 from 60.
Kenya Airways fell 45 cents to close at 7.05. Bourse officials said investors were willing to offload at whatever price they could get.
"I think most speculators especially those holding small lots ranging between 100 and 2,000 shares have decided to do away with the share completely," a broker said.
On the corporate bond board, one deal worth five million shillings was transacted pegged to Wednesday's treasury bill rate of 21.8 percent at a price of 101.43 percent.
